name: proofs
topic: two loaves cut the same morning, and a claim about which was fermented longer
why_this_fixture: The twin. It shares no noun, no capability, no evidence id and no refusal kind with
`moorings.json`, and it traverses the identical production path.
It is deliberately a DIFFERENT SHAPE as well as a different subject, because two fixtures that
differ only in vocabulary would prove that the composer ignores nouns and nothing else:
- no evidence here is of kind `extent`, so nothing in it can reach `visible`;
- the capability matrix is ABSENT rather than empty, so the gap list alone governs and a
measurement on an undeclared capability still counts — which is the branch `moorings`
- its accepted relation is REFUTED where the twin's is merely withheld, and it has no
unanchored reading, no dangling hypothesis and no broken plan citation at all.
If the refusals were hard-coded rather than derived, this fixture would report the twin's.
prompt: Two loaves cut the same morning. I think the second was fermented longer — say where the cut faces agree with that and where they do not.

images.title: the first loaf, cut face on
the second loaf, cut face on

hypotheses.statement: the second loaf was fermented longer than the first
both were raised from the same levain

observations.statement: the crumb opens into large irregular cells through the upper third of the face
the crust carries a single deep blister close to the seam
the cells run finer and more even across the whole face
the boule kept the ridging of the banneton through the bake
the lamination at the base has pulled apart in one place

alignments.statement: an open irregular crumb is what a long ferment tends to leave behind
an even fine field is the opposite of what the proposal predicts for the second

contrast_plans.statement: set the open upper third of the first face against the even field of the second
contrast_plans.because: the same question asked of two faces cut the same way

accepted_relations.statement: the first face is more open than the second
the second was fermented longer than the first
the blister sits where the seam was weakest

rejected_relations.statement: the two were raised from one levain

critiques.because: both faces were read for cell size and the two readings order the same way
cell area is not a clock; the same field follows from a warmer room and a shorter rise

observables.statement: how deep the blister runs beneath the surface
where the seam meets the cut face

capability_gaps.why: no producer here recovers a depth from a single photograph
nothing in a still frame carries elapsed time
nothing here reads the oven, and nothing in this inquiry asked it to
